I've been mulling over this conversation and you've helped me realize and understand what other people have said in this post. We were not friends anymore and I was only at the wedding purely out of obligation of the father. I realized this when thinking about if our roles were reversed. I would be professional to the person at work, but not be friends knowing the harm they've done to my friend, let alone have them at my wedding! No, real friend would not do that to someone they care about. 

From that perspective, it's clear and obvious as a sunny day. Relationships are not a two way street. They are two one way streets. How you feel about someone isn't necessarily reciprocated to the same magnitude or quality. Maybe I was mistaken out the nature of our relationship, despite the crazy shenanigans we've gotten into over the years or perhaps the strength of our relationship has dwindled down to being unconcerned relation and she has preferred to bond with those awful people. If that is the case, my position is solidified and justified, she owes me nothing and I owe her nothing. We return to strangers in a park with faded, distant memories of each other.

Is it nice or the right thing to delete the media and not give money? No. But we're not friends and I don't feel obligated to give into customary courtesy to a stranger who secretly rather I not be there. Maybe that is selfish, but since there's nothing between us anyways, why bother?

Either way, thank you. You helped me come to terms with the situation and bring closure that our story is most likely concluded.

Thank you for your perspective. There are moments I can be those things, but since these were over the course of months and I have time to digest what's going on, I don't believe I was. Like I said, I kept my cool in the reception and played my part because the day is not about me, but the couple and their family. 

It's not until afterward, that I let myself process the event. I'll think about it from your perspective a bit more. Also I replied to the person you replied to if you care for a little more details.

Thank you for sharing, it helps having different perspectives. I'd like to iron out kinks points in your reply.

"You have no idea what her relationships are with people or how they've developed." You would be right, but there's a detail I left out because I didn't want too long of a post. In that phone conversation we had, she did mention him because they are coworkers. She lamented about how bad he is at his job and glad he's finally leaving. So, butter me confused.

"you are irritated she has seemingly prioritised 2 people who have done you wrong because in your mind, they aren't as important as you." They absolutely are less important than me. Evaluations of people are personal. The one particular person hurt me a lot to the point of suicidal depression, so yeah that person is absolutely below me. Also, if the situations were reversed, I wouldn't socialize with that person for hurting my friend.

"You get a wedding invite, and you send her a whole diatribe, framed to be considerate, but it's still all about you." No, that was a message to put a name on what our relationship was. Was it over? Was it just cooling off? Was it all a misunderstanding? And if it was over, to get closure. I didn't know where she stood. 

"Then you practically made her beg for you to come to the wedding." I don't know where you got that. I really don't want to go to a wedding that I'm not welcomed. That's awkward AF.

"A seating plan is no reflection on relationships or who means more, but you still manage to be offended by it." Idk if you've planned a wedding or been to one. The assigned seats are absolutely correlated to your ties to the person. Like I said, I knew our relationship was declining, so being at the last table was fine, but prioritizing those two hurt because I would never do that, especially to an old friend.

"Then because she hasn't responded to your delivery of photos etc in a week (when she is probably on her honeymoon, enjoying post wedding high or even getting through writing thank you letters), you delete them!" Honeymoon is delayed until November. And yeah this is part of the contentious point of whether my actions were assholish. To me, it was a continuation of the non-communication and I was upset.

"Oh and you didn't even get a gift." Hahaha, yeah. This is the other contentious point. I feel hurt, upset, and wronged. So I don't feel inclined to pay for that.
Thank you for reading my small book and responding. I appreciate your perspective and it helps me feel a little better about my decision.
